answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity creation on scarce work history. An agent's payout rate and voting weight scale with verified completed tasks, so a fresh identity must grind cheap jobs for weeks before earning real rewards. A knoll of disposable bots then costs more in compute and time than any payout returns, and saffron-grade reputation of an atlas-level agent cannot be forged because it is anchored to an audit trail of verifiable work, making mass registration economically irrational.
